ai.literal: Indeed like humans resemble the base people; such a resemblance as them, we have seen not.
ai.translation: The base resemble human beings; we have never seen another similarity so perfect as that.
ai.modern: கீழ்மக்கள் மனிதர்களைப் போலவே இருக்கிறார்கள்; அவர்களைப் போன்ற ஒரு முழுமையான ஒற்றுமையை நாம் எங்கும் கண்டதில்லை.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the deceptive appearance of ignoble or base people. Outwardly, they look exactly like normal human beings, showing no physical difference. The poet humorously remarks that he has never seen such a perfect resemblance between two entirely different entities as that between the base and true humans. This serves as a warning that outward appearance is completely unreliable when judging a person's character.

ai.literal: Than those who know goodness, base people possess fortune; they do not have sorrow in their heart.
ai.translation: Base people are more fortunate than those who know what is good, for they have no worries or anxieties in their hearts.
ai.modern: நன்மையை அறிந்து நடப்பவர்களை விடக் கீழ்மக்கள் பேறு பெற்றவர்கள்; ஏனெனில் அவர்கள் தங்கள் நெஞ்சத்தில் எந்தக் கவலையும் இல்லாதவர்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet uses irony to contrast those who strive to live virtuously with base individuals. People who understand goodness and moral duty are often burdened by empathy and the anxiety of doing the right thing. In contrast, base people are described as fortunate because they completely lack a conscience. Since they do not care about right or wrong, they are entirely free from mental worry and sorrow in their hearts.

ai.literal: Gods are like the base; they too, themselves, things they desire doing, because of behaving.
ai.translation: The base are like the gods, because they too act exactly as they desire, without any restraint.
ai.modern: கயவர்கள் தேவர்களைப் போன்றவர்கள்; ஏனெனில், அவர்களும் தங்களுக்கு விருப்பமானவற்றையே செய்து வாழ்கிறார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet employs brilliant irony to compare base, unprincipled people to celestial beings. The poet states that the base resemble gods because both act entirely according to their own desires, free from any external control. While gods act out of supreme freedom and goodness, the base act solely to satisfy their impulses, completely unrestrained by moral codes. The key word 'மேவன' refers to things desired, and 'ஒழுகலான்' explains that this comparison is based on their unrestrained conduct.

ai.literal: A submissive person those who become if they see, than them exceedingly behaving, will swell with pride the base person.
ai.translation: If base people see those who submit to them, they will behave with even greater excess and swell with pride over them.
ai.modern: தமக்கு அடங்கி நடப்பவர்களைக் கண்டால், கீழ் மக்கள் அவர்களை விடவும் அதிகமாகத் தலைக்கனம் கொண்டு செருக்குடன் நடப்பார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet describes the arrogant nature of base or low-minded individuals when they encounter submissive people. When a base person (கீழ்) sees someone who is compliant or yields to them (அகப்பட்டி ஆவாரை), they do not show mercy or kindness. Instead, they behave with even greater dominance and arrogance (மிகப்பட்டு), swelling with pride (செம்மாக்கும்) to lord over them. Their power trip is triggered by the helplessness or submission of others, revealing their lack of true nobility.

ai.literal: Fear indeed of the base people is the conduct; the rest, if desire exists, will arise a little.
ai.translation: Fear alone is the rule of conduct for the base; other than that, a little good behavior may arise only if they desire some gain.
ai.modern: அச்சம் மட்டுமே கீழ்மக்களின் ஒழுக்கத்திற்குக் காரணம்; அது தவிர, ஏதேனும் நன்மை பெற வேண்டும் என்ற ஆசை இருந்தால் மட்டுமே அவர்களிடம் சிறிதளவு நல்லொழுக்கம் உண்டாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet analyzes the motivation of base or low-minded individuals. It states that fear (அச்சம்) is the primary force that drives them to maintain any discipline or proper conduct (ஆசாரம்). If they ever exhibit any other decent behavior (எச்சம்), it is not out of a sense of duty or virtue, but only when they have a selfish desire (அவா) for personal gain, and even then, such behavior is shown only in a very small measure (சிறிது).

ai.literal: Beaten drum like are the base people themselves, because of carrying and telling to others the secrets they heard.
ai.translation: The base are like a beaten drum, for they carry and blab to others every secret they happen to hear.
ai.modern: கீழ்மக்கள் தாங்கள் கேட்ட இரகசியங்களைப் பிறரிடம் கொண்டுபோய்ச் சொல்வதால், அவர்கள் அடிக்கப்படும் பறை போன்றவர்கள் ஆவர்.
ai.explanation: This couplet compares untrustworthy, base individuals to a beaten drum. A drum, when struck, loudly broadcasts its sound to everyone in the vicinity, keeping nothing to itself. Similarly, base people cannot contain any confidential information or secrets they happen to hear. They immediately carry and reveal these secrets to others, proving themselves completely incapable of maintaining trust.

ai.literal: Wet hand will not shake base people jaw breaking clenched-fisted-ones except to those.
ai.translation: Mean people will not even shake the leftover food from their wet hands for anyone, except for those who would break their jaws with a clenched fist.
ai.modern: கயவர்கள் தங்களுக்குக் குத்துவிடக் கை ஓங்கும் வன்முறையாளர்களுக்கு அன்றி, மற்றவர்களுக்குத் தாங்கள் சாப்பிட்டு முடித்த ஈரக் கையைக்கூட உதற மாட்டார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet satirizes the nature of base or mean-minded people. They are so utterly miserly that they will not even shake the moisture or leftover food grains from their wet hands to help a needy person. However, they will readily yield and give away everything to those who threaten them with clenched fists and are ready to break their jaws. The poet contrasts the utter stinginess of the base towards the polite with their instant submission to physical force.

ai.literal: Upon merely being told, the noble will be of use; like sugarcane, upon being crushed, the base will yield benefit.
ai.translation: Noble people will help as soon as they are told of one's need; but the base, like sugarcane, will yield only when they are crushed and squeezed.
ai.modern: தங்கள் குறையைச் சொன்னவுடனேயே சான்றோர் உதவி செய்வர்; ஆனால் கரும்பைப் பிழிவது போல நசுக்கிப் பிழிந்தால்தான் கீழ்மக்கள் உதவுவார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet contrasts the generous nature of noble people with the stubbornness of the base. Noble people (சான்றோர்) require only a simple request (சொல்ல) to motivate them to help. In contrast, a base person (கீழ்) is compared to sugarcane (கரும்பு), which does not give up its sweetness easily. Just as sugarcane must be crushed and squeezed (கொல்ல) in a mill to yield its juice, the base person will only be of use when subjected to force, pressure, or harsh treatment.

ai.literal: Clothing and food if they see, upon others fault to find capable will become the base person.
ai.translation: If a base person sees others enjoying decent clothing and food, they will immediately find faults in them out of sheer envy.
ai.modern: பிறர் நல்ல ஆடை உடுத்துவதையும் நல்ல உணவு உண்பதையும் கண்டால், அவர்கள் மீது குற்றம் கண்டுபிடிக்க வல்லவர் ஆவர் கீழ்மைக் குணம் உடையவர்.
ai.explanation: This couplet describes the deep-seated envy of base individuals (கீழ்). When they observe others enjoying basic comforts like clothing (உடுப்பது) and food (உண்பது), they cannot tolerate their prosperity. Driven by jealousy, they actively seek out faults or blemishes (வடு) in them. The word 'வற்று' denotes capability, showing that the only skill a low-minded person possesses is finding flaws in those who are doing well.

ai.literal: For what are they fit, the base people? If a crisis occurs, to sell themselves they are fit, quickly.
ai.translation: For what indeed are base people fit? If a crisis occurs, they are fit only to sell themselves in haste.
ai.modern: கீழ்மக்கள் எதற்குப் பயன்படுவார்கள்? ஒரு துன்பம் வந்தால், தங்களை விரைந்து விற்றுவிடுவதற்கு மட்டுமே அவர்கள் தகுதியானவர்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet satirizes the absolute worthlessness and lack of integrity of base people. The poet asks a rhetorical question: what are these low-minded people actually useful for? He answers with sharp irony: if any crisis or difficulty occurs, they will not stand by anyone or maintain their self-respect. Instead, they are only fit to quickly sell themselves out for personal gain or survival. The contrast between 'for what are they fit' and 'fit to sell themselves' highlights their complete lack of character.
